conceptual assets.information: The operational enable state determines whether the SPI engine, FIFO contents, clock generation, and related outputs are active. The SPI control use depends on this state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes the enable state at line 140. Availability is at risk because the state clears both FIFOs at lines 211 and 243, controls engine activation at line 281, and drives the clock-enable output at line 383.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write the control register to disable the SPI engine, clear queued data, and suppress further clock generation.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler, divider, and high-speed settings determine when the SPI engine advances and therefore the serial transfer rate. SPI timing operation depends on these settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus data writes the rate settings at lines 143 through 145. Availability is at risk because these settings control clock-enable generation and transfer progress at lines 371 through 377 and 299 through 317.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could change the prescaler, divider, or high-speed setting to slow, stall, or otherwise disrupt SPI transfers.

conceptual assets.information: The transmit payload is the byte written by the bus and shifted out over the SPI data output. SPI communication depends on delivering this payload to the selected peripheral.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the payload is carried to the externally observable spi_dat_o output at line 343. Integrity is at risk because bus data enters the transmit path at line 213 and is loaded and shifted by the transceiver at lines 292 and 318.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the serial output or alter the bus-written payload before it is transmitted.

conceptual assets.information: The receive payload is sampled from the SPI data input and returned to the bus through the receive FIFO. Software use of the peripheral depends on preserving the received byte.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because received data can be exposed through bus_rsp_o.data at line 174. Integrity is at risk because spi_dat_i is sampled at line 310 and the resulting value is shifted and stored through line 318 before being returned.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject or alter the serial input data, or read received payloads through the bus response.

conceptual assets.information: The chip-select state specifies whether a chip select is active and which of the eight external SPI devices is selected. SPI transfers depend on addressing the intended peripheral.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a queued control word changes cs_ctrl at line 290. Availability is at risk because cs_ctrl determines whether and which spi_csn_o bit is asserted at lines 353 and 354, so an altered state can block or misroute transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject a chip-select command that selects the wrong peripheral or leaves the intended peripheral inactive.

conceptual assets.information: A marker in a queued transmit word selects whether the word changes chip-select state or is serialized as payload data. Correct interpretation of queued words depends on this decision.
